result.topic_en: Draft notes, written on a printed postal ledger form, characterizing algebraic functions by their behaviour near branch points and infinity points: in the neighbourhood of such points they can be expanded in fractional and negative powers, with logarithmic and polar terms.

methods.what: Near a non-branch pole an algebraic function can be made continuous by subtracting a finite principal part (Laurent polar terms)
methods.quote: Zweig der Function durch Subtraction [-einer ganzen Function ... von der Form $(z-s)$-] $\frac{a}{z-s}+\frac{b}{(z-s)^2}$ ... in eine stetige Function

methods.what: The integral of an algebraic function near a non-branch point equals a logarithmic term plus polar terms plus a regular power series
At branch points one substitutes the local uniformizer $(z-s)^{1/\mu}$, and at infinity $1/z$
methods.quote:

und wenn $s$ unendlich ist $z-s$ durch $\frac{1}{z}$.

items.english: An algebraic function that becomes infinite at a point of the surface S where z = s can, if this point is not a branch point, by these theorems be transformed by subtraction into a function continuous at that point.
